texts.li: [lowtech,tale] {X_nameDef}, a wandering bard of {FACTION}, would like supper and a bed for the night, and will pay in songs and tales, as bards do. {X_nameDef} has already heard of this colony. On the road, the story goes like this: "{TALE}"
[lowtech,notale] {X_nameDef}, a wandering bard of {FACTION}, has come to spend an evening at the colony, trading tales and songs for supper and a bed, as bards always have.

[!lowtech,tale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a traveling storyteller with a battered instrument and a hundred stories, is stopping for the night. {X_nameDef} already knows a story about this colony, and tells it like this: "{TALE}"
[notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the colony with a pack full of songs and a head full of tall tales. {X_nameDef} would like a meal and a place to sleep, and will pay in stories tonight.

[tale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who tells stories for a living, has come to spend the night. {X_nameDef} has a new favorite, picked up on the road, about this very colony: "{TALE}" Tonight, {X_nameDef} promises, everyone gets the long version.

[!lowtech,notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a traveling storyteller with a battered instrument and a hundred stories, is stopping for the night. There will be stories after supper for anyone who stays up.

lines.li: ...and that's why you never trust a muffalo...
...on the far side of the mountains...

texts.li: Travelers from {FACTION} are on their way to the colony to visit the grave of {DEAD}. They knew {DEAD} long before the colony did, as family or close to it. They'll stand at the grave for a while, and then go.
[lowtech] Word of {DEAD}'s death traveled farther than anyone thought. Kin from {FACTION} are walking in to pay their respects at the grave, as their custom is.
[!lowtech] Someone from {FACTION} found {DEAD}'s name in a settlement record and has come all this way with family to see the grave. They won't stay long.

lines.li: Thank you for looking after them.

texts.li: [lowtech] A small band of pilgrims of {FACTION}, footsore and thin, is walking up to the colony. Their road is long and their bags are empty, and they ask, very politely, for a meal before they go on.
[!lowtech] A handful of pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped outside the colony on their way somewhere they hope will be better. Their rations ran out three days ago, and they'd be grateful for a meal.

On the long walk to a place holy to them, pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped by the colony. They carry very little and have eaten less, and ask if the colony can spare a meal. They'll pray for the colony in return.
[winter] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come in out of the cold, half frozen and very hungry, asking for a hot meal and somewhere warm to sit before they go on.

li.label: Feed them
li.outcome: The pilgrims eat everything they're given and thank their hosts twice over. They'll speak well of the colony to everyone they meet on the road.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The pilgrims bow, and go on hungry.

li.label: Bread for the road, no more
li.outcome: The pilgrims get a loaf each and a full waterskin, and go on before dark. It isn't a meal, but they thank the colony for it.

outcomes.li: [winter] A loaf each and a hot drink at the gate, then back on the road. The pilgrims bow and go on into the cold.
[colony:Thrifty] Bread for the road and nothing more, as the colony's habit is. The pilgrims take it gratefully all the same.

texts.li: [tribal] {X_nameDef}, a lore-keeper of {FACTION} who carries a whole people's history in {X_possessive} head, asks for a place to sleep tonight. When {X_nameDef} hears the colony is working on {TALE}, {X_pronoun} smiles. There's an old story about that, and it might help.

[lowtech,!tribal] {X_nameDef}, a wandering scholar of {FACTION} with ink-stained fingers and a satchel of books, asks for a bed for the night. On hearing that the colony is working on {TALE}, {X_nameDef} starts asking questions, and doesn't stop until supper is cleared away.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a traveling engineer of {FACTION}, asks for a bunk for the night. Someone mentions the colony's work on {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} immediately asks to see the notes. "Oh, no, no, no," {X_nameDef} says, smiling. "Let me show you."

li.label: Host {X_objective} for the night
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} talk until the small hours. By morning, the colony's work on {TALE} is a good deal further along.

li.label: No room tonight
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs and moves on to the next settlement.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to teach everyone instead
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} held a lesson after supper for anyone who'd sit still for it. The notes on {TALE} only grew by a page, but everyone who stayed up learned something.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} drew letters and sums in the ashes of the hearth until late, and the colony copied them onto slates. {A_nameDef} asked the most questions.
[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} turned the dining table into a classroom for the evening, with a chalk board propped on a chair. The work on {TALE} moved a little, the colony a good deal more.

texts.li: A young traveler named {X_nameDef} has come a long way to find {A_nameDef}. Word of {A_nameDef}'s skill at {SKILL} has spread farther than anyone here knew, and {X_nameDef} wants to learn from the best. {X_nameDef} asks to stay as {A_nameDef}'s apprentice.
[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, barely grown, has turned up asking for {A_nameDef}, the master of {SKILL} the whole valley talks about. {X_nameDef} will work for board and lessons, and asks to stay.

li.label: Take {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a student now, and has already started on the first lesson.

li.label: Send {X_objective} home
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes, disappointed. {A_nameDef} is quieter than usual that evening.

texts.li: A stranger called {X_nameDef} has been waiting outside the colony since dawn, and asks to stay. {X_nameDef} answers every question politely and none of them fully. Where from? "Far." Why here? "Why not?" {A_nameDef} thinks {X_nameDef} is running from trouble, and also looks like a hard worker.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} walked out of the wilds with good boots, empty hands and a name that might be real. {X_nameDef} asks to stay, asks nothing about anyone here, and would rather not talk about the past. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} first.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} walked in off the road with a good coat, no papers and a story that changes slightly every time it's told. {X_nameDef} asks to stay. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} first, and thinks there's more to the story.

li.label: Take the stranger in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is one of us now. Whatever {X_pronoun} left behind, {X_pronoun} hasn't said.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} talk to {X_objective} first
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat {X_nameDef} down by the gate and talked until {X_nameDef} had told enough of it. {X_nameDef} is one of us now, with nothing left to hide.

outcomes.li: [past:outlaw] {A_nameDef} knew the right questions, having once had to dodge them. {X_nameDef} answered them all, and is one of us now.

li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} talked with {X_nameDef} most of the afternoon and came back satisfied. {X_nameDef} is one of us now, though {A_nameDef} isn't sure {X_nameDef} told all of it.

texts.li: A child has wandered into the colony: {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, muddy, scared and very far from home. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} sitting by the fields, trying hard not to cry. Somewhere out there, a family is searching.

[winter] {A_nameDef} found a child out in the cold, half frozen and too frightened to speak. It's {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, who wandered off from {X_possessive} people and couldn't find the way back. {X_nameDef}'s family must be searching.

li.label: Take {X_objective} home
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is walked back toward {X_possessive} people, clutching a bit of bread and somebody's spare coat. {FACTION} won't forget this.

li.label: Keep {X_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stays, though no one asked what {X_pronoun} wanted. For the first few nights, {X_nameDef} cries for home.

texts.li: A stray {THING} has followed {A_nameDef} all the way home and refuses to leave {A_possessive} side. It's thin, it's filthy, and it has very clearly decided {A_nameDef} is its person now.

[child] A stray {THING} followed {A_nameDef} home, and {A_nameDef} has already given it a name, a bowl and a corner of {A_possessive} bed. The look on {A_possessive} face says the matter is not up for discussion.
[hunter] A scrawny stray {THING} has been hanging around {A_nameDef} all day, bringing small dead things as gifts. It seems to think the colony could use a hunter.

li.label: It can stay
li.outcome: The {THING} curls up at {A_nameDef}'s feet as if it had always lived here.

li.label: Let it go
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks the {THING} to the edge of the fields and leaves it there. It sits and watches {A_objective} go.
